svg.text: Service & server infrastructure security — current state and roadmap (updated)

foreignObject.div: Internet

UFW firewall — done
Default deny, only required ports open

fail2ban — planned
Watches auth logs, bans into UFW

Nginx — done
TLS termination, routes by port / path

Platform + app services (Docker)
One public port per service today

Kubernetes services
Exposed via NodePort

Critical gap found: Docker + Kubernetes NodePorts bypass UFW entirely.
Docker/kube-proxy write DNAT rules directly into iptables (FORWARD chain) before traffic ever reaches UFW's INPUT-chain policy. A container/NodePort published on 0.0.0.0 is reachable from the internet regardless of UFW's allow/deny state. Discovered via a backend (port 8006) that stayed open even after its UFW rule was deleted.

Fixed this session: 11 Docker-published backends firewalled via DOCKER-USER chain
Platform UI, ALIS, Auth, Grafana, Infisical, kg-service, MCP (x2), Uptime Kuma, Hypothesis API, bio-semantic-parser. Rules match the post-DNAT container IP:port, scoped to the public interface only — verified nginx access unaffected (baseline vs. after comparison on every path). Full detail: port-security-hardening-notes.md.

Pending: Galaxy (port 9094) — not found in Docker's port list; may be a native process or a --network host container (looks identical from outside). Exposure mechanism unconfirmed — needs lsof -i :9094 before deciding UFW vs. iptables fix.

Not yet fixed: 5 Kubernetes NodePorts still directly public
Ports 30501/30502/30503/30504 (Annotation, AI Assistant, two unlabeled services) and 30443 (Kubernetes Dashboard). No Docker-style admin override chain exists for kube-proxy, and kube-proxy re-syncs its own rules — a naive copy of the Docker fix risks silently no-op'ing.

Planned fix: convert Service type NodePort → ClusterIP
Removes the public port entirely rather than firewalling around kube-proxy. Nginx (running on the same cluster node) proxies directly to the ClusterIP, matching the same "single door through nginx" pattern already used for Docker services. Add nginx path (e.g. dev.rejuve.bio/kubernetes) for consolidation together with this change — the path alone does not close the NodePort.

Gap: 20+ public ports, one per service (separate from the exposure bug above — these are intentionally nginx-fronted). Planned: consolidate to path-/subdomain-based routing behind 443 where the app supports being served from a subpath.

Risk: tonight's iptables rules are not persistent. A reboot silently reopens all 11 fixed services — no alert. Needs iptables-persistent/netfilter-persistent or a startup unit before this can be considered done.
Nginx (from section 1)

Current: direct public route
Infisical, K8s dashboard, Grafana, Kuma — only their own app login gates access

Infisical
Secrets store

K8s dashboard
Cluster control — highest blast radius

Grafana / Kuma
Monitoring UIs

Planned: auth gateway — IP allowlist or oauth2-proxy, ideally VPN-only.
Quick-win: Tailscale already installed on this host — scope nginx allow/deny to the Tailscale range for these four services instead of building oauth2-proxy from scratch.

g.text: Priority: fix Kubernetes Dashboard first — dashboard compromise = full cluster compromise.

Promtail — done
Ships logs from hosts

Loki — done
Log storage

Scrapes metrics

Metrics storage — done
Time-series data

Grafana — done
Dashboards, single access point

Gap: coverage check needed
Confirm UFW, SSH auth, fail2ban events flow into pipeline

New — planned: firewall drop logging. Add an iptables LOG rule just before each DOCKER-USER DROP, so probes against the now-blocked ports (8006, 3009, 3002, etc.) surface in Loki/Grafana instead of vanishing silently.

g.text: Note: Grafana is also reached through the admin/secrets path in section 2 — the planned auth gateway applies here too.

foreignObject.div: Code commit

div.span: cosign signing before deploy (corrected: previously listed as planned)

g.text: Correction from prior version: secret scanning and cosign image signing are both already implemented.

foreignObject.div:
SSH hardening — planned
Key-only authentication, disable password auth. Complements the planned fail2ban (section 1) — fail2ban slows brute force, disabling password auth removes the attack surface outright.

Automatic OS security updates — planned
unattended-upgrades for the host OS, independent of the CI/CD pipeline's application-layer scanning (section 4).
Reminder: persistence gap from section 1 applies here too — any host-hardening step should be paired with confirming it (and the DOCKER-USER rules) survive a reboot before being marked "done."

svg.text: Diagram reflects state as of 2026-07-05, including the port-exposure audit performed this session (11 backends fixed via DOCKER-USER; Galaxy and 5 Kubernetes NodePorts pending).
Blue "fixed this session" items are new since the prior version of this diagram. Amber/red items are proposed next steps, not yet built.
